Front: Why is weighted-avg F1 misleading on an imbalanced dataset; what is the honest headline?
Back: Weighted-avg F1 averages per-class F1 by support, so the majority class dominates - you can score high just by nailing the common class. Use macro-F1 (unweighted mean of per-class F1) as the headline; it weights every class equally and exposes minority-class failures.

Front: Why are class weights 1/n and N/n the same training objective?
Back: They differ only by the global constant N (= total count). CrossEntropyLoss(weight=w, reduction='mean') normalizes by the sum of weights, so a global constant cancels. Only the RATIOS between class weights matter; any global scale washes out. Same loss -> same gradients -> same model.

Front: Why select configs on validation and touch test only once?
Back: Validation is the scratchpad for comparing/selecting. If you select based on test, that number stops being an unbiased generalization estimate (you fit to it). Every peek-and-adjust leaks optimism, so test is used once, at the end, on the already-chosen model.

Front: What is the effective-number-of-samples idea (Cui et al. class-balanced weighting)?
Back: Samples overlap as a class grows, so each new one adds less information; the effective number E_n = (1-beta^n)/(1-beta) saturates. Weighting by 1/E_n down-weights the majority class SOFTLY, unlike the brutal 1/n. beta dials between no weighting (0) and inverse-frequency (1).

Front: Controlled comparison finding: did loss weighting improve macro-F1 on MIT-BIH?
Back: No. In a fair comparison (fixed seed, val selection), aggressive schemes (inverse, sqrt_inverse) degraded and destabilized macro-F1; class_balanced (0.862) landed within noise of unweighted (0.858). The earlier 'it helped' was uncontrolled-run variance. Weighting shifts the precision/recall profile toward recall, but is not a macro-F1 win.

Front: What actually pushes macro-F1 higher on imbalanced ECG (since weighting did not)?
Back: More epochs, a deeper model with residual/skip connections, and minority-class data augmentation (add noise/scale/shift) - attacking imbalance at the DATA level. Kachuee et al. use all three. Loss weighting alone is not the lever.
